thread.title: Apple earnings arrive amid iPhone doubts and FaceTime bug: Live blog

author: Jeremy C. Owens, Emily Bary
title: Apple earnings arrive amid iPhone doubts and FaceTime bug: Live blog
text:
Apple Inc. has already warned that it will post disappointing results for the holiday season, but there’s still plenty to be gleaned from the company’s earnings report Tuesday afternoon.
Chief Executive Tim Cook cited weakness in China as a key reason for Apple’s AAPL, -1.04% revenue miss in the December period, and the key question is how long the company’s problems there will persist. Apple’s March-quarter outlook will serve as a good initial barometer for the company’s view of the global smartphone landscape. For the first time, investors won’t receive information about iPhone unit sales or the average selling prices of Apple devices. The company has done away with those metrics , prompting concerns about the health of the iPhone business, and will instead report services margins as the company tries to direct attention toward this fast-growing area of the business and away from the more troubled hardware categories.
Look for commentary on how the economic slowdown in China is affecting the App Store and other components of the services segment, as well as a FaceTime bug that was revealed Monday and inadvertently allowed users to eavesdrop on other people’s smartphone microphones.
The results for Apple’s fiscal first quarter are expected to arrive at 4:30 p.m. Eastern time, and the company’s conference call with analysts kicks off at 5 p.m. MarketWatch senior editor Jeremy C. Owens ( @jowens510 ) and tech reporter Emily Bary ( @emilybary ) will be breaking down the results here on our live blog.
